A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PSFT research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning, RL and human-alignment experiments, including benchmark scores, training dynamics and clipping analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original multimodal, coding, larger-model, baseline and ablation results.

M1.justification: The core clipped objective, gradient, evolving reference policy and optional warm-up remain unchanged. v2 adds experimental PSFT-Ent variants restricting updates to high-entropy tokens (Appendix C.2), and a VLM adaptation that trains the language component while freezing multimodal components (C.7.4).

E1.justification: v2 extends the original mathematics and human-alignment coverage to visual reasoning and coding. Added coverage includes Geometry-3K training, MathVerse, MathVista, MMMU and MMMU-Pro evaluation, and OpenR1-code training with LiveCodeBench evaluation (Section 4.4 and Appendix C.6).

E2.justification: iw-SFT and DFT, only discussed in v1, become evaluated comparators in v2 Table 9 and Figure 12. The new VLM comparison also includes RL directly from the base model. The original SFT and SFT-KL comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Original math, RL and alignment configurations are retained. New experiments introduce a Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE model, reference-update intervals, learning-rate controls, and VLM-specific training settings, including a 6k cutoff and 5k RL response limit (Section 5.3 and Appendices C.3, C.5 and C.7).

E4.justification: Beyond the retained warm-up, clipped-token and clipping-threshold analyses, v2 tests fixed versus periodically updated reference policies, high-entropy token selection, and learning-rate sensitivity. Appendix C.9 adds a geometry case comparing base-model reasoning and PSFT responses with and without reasoning.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing avg@32 and avg@8 evaluation conventions remain, and the added results continue to use point estimates and training curves without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original result Tables 1–5 retain their values in v2 Tables 1–3. Substantial new results cover VLMs, coding, MoE models, baselines and ablations; for example, v2 Table 8 reports MoE IFEval scores of 88.52 for PSFT and 50.56 for SFT. These are newly reported evaluations, not performance gains over the original runs.

T1.justification: v1 derives the objective and clipped gradient but contains no convergence theorem. v2 Appendix C.1 adds smoothness and bounded-gradient assumptions, Theorem 1 claiming O(1/sqrt(T)) convergence, and a multi-step proof. The proof does not establish its asserted smoothness at the hard-clipping boundary.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction explicitly extend applicability from mathematics and human-value alignment to multimodal tasks. The central contributions—preserving general capabilities, avoiding entropy collapse and improving subsequent RL/DPO optimization—remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes the offline supervised objective from on-policy PPO and adds interpretations of reference-update, learning-rate and multimodal-transfer results. Appendix A introduces concrete scale, diversity and architecture limitations, although its statement that MoE models remain untested contradicts the experiment in Appendix C.3.

D1.justification: Original configuration tables and system prompts are retained. v2 adds reference-update intervals, entropy thresholds, iw-SFT clipping settings, VLM configurations and code-data filtering details. It replaces the direct repository link with a supplementary-code statement and removes v1's Math-Verify preprocessing footnote, without establishing a change to the underlying preprocessing.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds a substantive discussion of hybrid SFT/RL approaches, including LUFFY and HPT, positioning PSFT as orthogonal to them. It reframes comparisons with iw-SFT and DFT around entropy and general-capability retention, removes the explicit GEM discussion, and adds literature supporting the new evaluation domains.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes and expands the preliminaries and method explanation, consolidates alignment subsections, moves evaluation descriptions into the appendix, and rewrites numerous findings paragraphs. The appendix is substantially reorganized, with additional reproducibility, ethics, limitations and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: v1 Tables 1–4 are merged and transposed into v2 Tables 1–2, while several training plots become compact combined panels. v2 adds numerous experiment and case-study displays, corrects percentage axes and a clipping legend, and extensively changes figure sizing, placement and text wrapping.

improvement.justification: The added iw-SFT/DFT comparisons, learning-rate controls and reference-policy ablations strengthen evidence that was missing in v1, while new domains broaden validation. However, the new convergence proof assumes smoothness of a hard-clipped objective and does not justify its conversion from a weighted gradient bound to the stated unweighted rate. The MoE limitation also contradicts the added experiment. These empirical gains and newly introduced correctness problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
